content.text:
The uninitialized field `runningBatchKey` existed from the very creation of `BddRunContext.java`. Since `putRunningBatch()` is only called during normal story-batch processing, any code path that calls `getRunningBatchKey()`/`getRunningBatch()` before that happens (e.g., when running under jbehave-junit-runner, which bypasses the normal batch embedder flow) would hit `Optional.empty()` and throw `IllegalStateException`. The fix simply gives the field a safe default (`"batch-1"`), which has been needed since the field's inception.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: aef6f032ea31d1d05104adf8560ca479cd27d8ad

## Reasoning
(1) I ran `git log --follow -p` on `BddRunContext.java` to trace the full history of the `runningBatchKey` field. The fix commit (1ea50f5) changes `private Optional<String> runningBatchKey;` to `private Optional<String> runningBatchKey = Optional.of("batch-1");` with the comment "must be initialized for jbehave-junit-runner". I then checked every prior commit touching this file to see when the field was declared without an initializer.

(2) The field was declared as `private Optional<String> runningBatchKey;` (no default value) at the moment the file was first created, in commit `aef6f032` ("new file ... BddRunContext.java"). None of the subsequent commits (`df5af23f`, `c9e5d872`, `c6b7e2d8`, `09fa1e43`) changed this declaration — they only touched unrelated imports/methods (batch storage refactoring, adding `getRunningBatchKey()` getter, etc.), always leaving the field uninitialized. So the uninitialized-field state traces directly back to the file's creation commit.

(3) Supporting evidence: `getRunningBatchKey()`/`getRunningBatch()` throw `IllegalStateException` when `runningBatchKey` is `Optional.empty()` (the default for an uninitialized `Optional` field is `null`, but once any code path calls `removeRunningBatch()` or the field is simply never populated, `.orElseThrow()` fires). Callers such as `AllureStoryReporter.java:158` and `VariablesFactory.java:67` invoke `getRunningBatchKey()` without necessarily guaranteeing `putRunningBatch()` was called first — which is exactly the jbehave-junit-runner scenario referenced in the fix's comment. The fix's new unit test `testGetDefaultRunningBatchKey()` directly asserts the field now defaults to `"batch-1"` without any setup call, confirming the bug was the lack of a sane default from the start.

I'm fairly confident in this attribution since the field's declaration is unchanged across all intermediate commits — there's no separate commit that "removed" an initializer; it was simply never present.
